sources.entry: Dashy - Feature-rich homepage for your homelab, with easy YAML configuration. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker
Dashy | Feature-rich homelab dashboard with status checks, widgets and themes

summary.one_liner: Dashy is a self-hosted, YAML-configured homepage and dashboard for homelabs that lists your apps and services with status checks, widgets, themes and search.
summary.what_it_does: Dashy lets you build a start page of links and apps, organized into sections and multiple pages, configured via a single YAML file (user-data/conf.yml) or edited live in its UI. Each item can have an icon from Font Awesome, Simple Icons, selfh.st, Material Icons, dashboard-icons, favicons, emojis, or local/URL images. It can check whether apps respond over HTTP and send ICMP pings to hosts, showing status indicators. It offers instant search by name, tag or hotkey, plus web search with custom bangs. Additional views include a minimal startpage view and a workspace view for multiple apps at once. Optional basic auth, OIDC/Keycloak SSO, and encrypted cloud backup are available.
use_cases: Shared family or team dashboard with user access controls
how_to_run: git clone the repo and cd dashy
notable: Single-file YAML configuration, also editable through the built-in UI with live preview
Multiple icon sources including favicons, homelab icons and Font Awesome
Launch methods include new tab, modal popup, workspace view and clipboard copy
Optional end-to-end encrypted cloud backup and restore
Available as Docker image on Docker Hub and GHCR, multi-arch amd64 and arm64
caveats: Bare-metal install requires a current Node LTS version and Yarn
Cloud backup is optional and relies on a Cloudflare worker backend
32-bit ARM is not supported in Docker
keywords: organize my bookmarks for self-hosted apps
show all my homelab services on one page
